result.response:
Implementation plan:
- Files:
  - core/health.py: Define a simple callable that returns {"status": "ok"}.
  - tests/test_health.py: Unit tests validating the health response shape and value.

Primary design decisions:
- Framework-agnostic core function (health) returning a plain dict to keep logic simple and portable. Any HTTP routing remains separate if/when a web framework layer exists.
- Pure function facilitates fast, deterministic unit tests without network/server bootstrapping.

Risks:
- If an existing web framework/router convention is required (e.g., FastAPI/Flask/Django), additional integration glue may be needed elsewhere.
- Naming collisions if core/health.py or health() already exist; adjust names accordingly.

```json

  "operations": [
    {
      "action": "create",
      "path": "core/health.py",
      "content": "def health():\n    \"\"\"Return a simple health status payload.\"\"\"\n    return {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n",
      "reason": "Add core health check callable returning the required payload"
    },
    {
      "action": "create",
      "path": "tests/test_health.py",
      "content": "from core.health import health\n\n\ndef test_health_returns_ok_exact_payload():\n    assert health() == {\"status\": \"ok\"}\n\n\ndef test_health_status_key_present_and_ok():\n    payload = health()\n    assert isinstance(payload, dict)\n    assert payload.get(\"status\") == \"ok\"\n",
      "reason": "Add unit tests to validate health response shape and value"
    }
  ]
}
```
